# Prompt Forge

> A public-domain visual prompt instrument. 2,032 signals across 16 creative
> axes. You build an image prompt by choosing at most one signal per axis, in
> service of a single stated idea.

License: CC0-1.0. No account, key, attribution, or permission required.
Homepage: https://androotandtheretinue.github.io/prompt-forge/

## Get the vocabulary

Do not scrape index.html. It is a 173 kB single-file application and the
signal pools begin about 34 kB in, past the point where many fetchers
truncate. Read one of these instead:

- https://androotandtheretinue.github.io/prompt-forge/vocabulary.json
- https://androotandtheretinue.github.io/prompt-forge/vocabulary.txt

Same content, generated from the application source. JSON carries the axis
metadata; the text file is flat and needs no parser.

## The 16 axes, in prompt order

narrative (story signal, 80), action (160), mood (144), composition (80),
setting (160), framing (camera, 128), wardrobe (144), medium (160),
style (176), lighting (128), palette (128), colorlogic (color logic, 80),
texture (128), weather (112), fx (128), quality (96).

## How to operate it

1. State the single idea the image is in service of. One sentence, in your
   own words, before choosing anything.
2. Choose at most one signal per axis, and only values listed under that
   axis. A signal is valid only in the axis that lists it. Several axes
   carry adjacent language, and relocating a value is the most common
   observed failure: "Twilight" is a lighting signal, and the weather axis
   does not contain it. Check the axis, not just the vocabulary.
3. Do not invent, translate, pluralize, abbreviate, or blend signals. If
   the idea wants something the vocabulary lacks, say so plainly rather
   than approximating it — a near-miss is indistinguishable from a real
   signal to whoever reads the prompt next.
4. Omit any axis that does not serve the idea. Filling all sixteen is the
   most common sign that a form is being completed rather than an image
   being made; six chosen signals beat sixteen supplied ones. Omission is
   a decision, not a gap, and you should be able to say why you omitted.
5. Emit the chosen signals in the axis order above.
6. Name the idea alongside the prompt, so a reader can judge whether the
   signals actually served it.

If you cannot reach the vocabulary files, say so and stop. Do not supply
remembered or plausible-sounding signals in their place.
